schema_note: Fixture allowlist for the synthtwin data-provenance guard (plan D13). Each entry in 'fixtures' binds one committed data fixture to its origin and must contain exactly these keys: 'path' (repository-relative POSIX path of the committed fixture file), 'generator' (repository-relative path of the seeded script that rebuilds the fixture; invoked as: python <generator> --seed <seed> --out <output-path>), 'seed' (integer seed; the same seed must always produce the same bytes on every platform), 'sha256' (64-character lowercase hex digest of the committed fixture bytes), and 'justification' (a written sentence explaining why this fixture must be committed instead of being built at test time). The checker tools/provenance/check_provenance.py re-runs every generator and byte-compares its output to the committed file; any difference fails. Both 'path' and 'generator' must be repository-relative (no absolute paths, no '..' components), must stay inside the repository, and must be tracked by git once the repository has commits. Generators are executed through tools/provenance/guard_runner.py, which installs a Python audit hook before the generator code runs; the hook refuses imports of network, process, and native-capability modules and blocks the known socket, process-creation, and native-call audit events. That runner is a best-effort in-process guard, not a sandbox or a confinement mechanism: repository source review of every generator script and the CI checks are the operative controls (CI is the authoritative automated verification; from Phase 3's visibility flip the branch ruleset makes it a mechanically enforced merge requirement - see SECURITY.md's activation record). JSON is treated as a data format: a tracked .json file is allowed only if it is one of the checker's known configuration files (KNOWN_CONFIG_JSON in the checker) or listed here. Committed fixtures must be tiny; the cap is the checker's own MAX_FIXTURE_BYTES, which carries the record of what it was raised from and why.
